general_information.Description: This unit will help students to develop the knowledge and skills necessary to identify and evaluate the key factors involved in making sound credit and lending decisions and to restructure credit proposals to meet the needs of both the borrower and lender. The unit includes the application of these principles to a series of practical lending situations: corporate customers, lending to small business… Throughout the unit, case studies are used to illustrate and develop the concepts and principles covered and to develop the students' credit appraisal skills. Case studies also figure prominently in the assessment for the unit.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Class attendance is strongly encouraged. Attend more than 80% of class hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course website (http://cms.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course, for online supports from teachers and other students and for practicing and assessment.

assessments.Question Type: Students are required to prepare a lending submission for an actual company.
assessments.Note: Each group has maximum of 3 people. All assignments should be typed and double-spaced with 11-point font, and must be submitted in both soft and hard copy in about 10-15 pages. A deduction of 10% of the assignment mark will be applied for each day of late submission; The deadline for the assignment submission is noticed in the syllabus schedule.

assessments.Question Type: Students should attend all the sessions and actively participate in class discussion for full credit.
assessments.Note: Participation grade will be given based on students' preparation, and quantity as well as quality of participation in classroom; quality of participation is demonstrated through asking relevant questions, making statements that add to and facilitate class discussion, and builds upon others’ comments. Class preparation and pre-reading before lecture will be assessed upon individuals' understanding and ability to answer questions in the class. Individuals will be called up randomly to be assessed.

schedule.Topic: Course introduction 1. THE PRINCIPLE OF LENDING AND LENDING BASICS - The principles of good lending - The lending process - Lending case study
Exercises
2. CONSUMER LENDING - Consumer lending - Real estate lending - Electronic banking: Visa credit
Exercises
3. CORPORATE AND BUSINESS LENDING - Corporate lending - Small business lending
Exercises

4. SPECIFIC LENDING PRINCIPLES – FIRST AND SECOND WAYS OUT Specific Lending Principles (i.e. first and second ways out): - The first way out (i.e. from cash flow from operations) - The second way out (i.e. security) - Why security is viewed as the second way out - More detailed ways of assessing a lending proposition
Exercises

5. DETAILED ASSESSMENT OF THE FIRST WAY OUT Detailed Assessment of the First Way Out - Analysis of historical financial information (B/S, P/L, Cash Flow Statements) - Analysis of financial projections (Cash Flow Budgets). More Advanced Analysis Of The First Way Out - Capital and its properties - Liquidity, solvency, and business performance analysis - Cash flow checklist
Exercises Progress test 1

6. PRACTICAL ISSUES TO DO WITH ANALYSIS OF THE SECOND WAY OUT - the common forms of security and their relative quality - the basic documentation - calculation of lending margins - potential tradeoffs between first and second ways out - other practical security issues
Exercises
7. A LENDING CASE STUDY - A case study to illustrate the analysis of the first way out. (financial analysis based on creditor' perspective)
Exercises Progess test 2
8. ANALYSIS AND INTERPRETATION OF CREDIT RISK - Risk analysis - Financial statements analysis - Credit scoring techniques
Exercises Essay Test
9. LENDING SUBMISSIONS - Writing a lending submission - Lending submission case study Introduction to Group Homework Assignment
10. MORE ADVANCED TOPICS IN LENDING - Guarantee - Factoring
10. MORE ADVANCED TOPICS IN LENDING (continue) - Import and Export financing
Course revision Group Homework Assignment Submission
